title: AbGen: Evaluating Large Language Models in Ablation Study Design and Evaluation for Scientific Research
authors: Yilun Zhao; Weiyuan Chen; Zhijian Xu; Manasi Patwardhan; Chengye Wang; Yixin Liu; Lovekesh Vig; Arman Cohan
task_description: Given a research context and a named module/process, generate a detailed ablation design; evaluate importance, faithfulness, soundness, and reliability of automated evaluators.
inputs: Expert-restructured paper context; named essential module or process; reference ablation design
outputs_or_labels: Ablation design; human ratings; meta-evaluation labels
pipeline_gap_filled: composition-level ablation design and evaluator calibration
evidence_basis: ACL abstract and paper: 2,000 expert-annotated examples from 677 NLP papers; task conditions on a specified module/process and includes AbGen-Eval.
limitations: Evaluates designs for ablations rather than executing a standardized end-to-end context-engine pipeline; domain is NLP papers.
why_relevant: Best methodology for defining component-removal matrices, preventing vague “remove one thing” tests, and calibrating automatic judges against expert assessment.

title: ERASER: A Benchmark to Evaluate Rationalized NLP Models
authors: Jay DeYoung; Sarthak Jain; Nazneen Fatema Rajani; Eric Lehman; Caiming Xiong; Richard Socher; Byron C. Wallace
task_description: Evaluate whether selected rationales are human-plausible and causally useful by running the predictor on the selected rationale and on the input with the rationale removed.
inputs: Documents or contexts; human rationale spans; model predictions
outputs_or_labels: Rationale precision/recall/F1; sufficiency; comprehensiveness; task score
evidence_basis: ACL paper defines sufficiency and comprehensiveness; comprehensiveness is measured with contrast inputs formed by removing predicted rationales.
limitations: Removal scores can be gamed by out-of-distribution complements; explanations need distribution-preserving controls and dependency-aware annotations.
why_relevant: Direct template for raw-vs-selected-vs-removed comparisons at extraction/selection/compression boundaries.

title: Multi-View Source Ablation for Faithful Summarization
authors: Shuyang Cao; Liang Ma; Di Lu; Robert L. Logan IV; Joel Tetreault; Alejandro Jaimes
task_description: Create multiple source views by masking or removing information, then score each generated summary token by the change in generation probability between original and ablated source.
inputs: Source document; generated summary; entity-masked or otherwise ablated source views
outputs_or_labels: Token-level ablation sensitivity; faithfulness score; human correlation
artifact_access_status: paper_and_PDF_accessible; code not confirmed in inspected evidence
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly describes multi-view source ablation and probability differences, with AggreFact alignment.
limitations: Token probability sensitivity is not a proof/dependency graph and can reflect model uncertainty rather than causal use.
why_relevant: Reusable multi-view intervention pattern for testing whether claims survive source-unit removal, including entity, qualifier, and citation-span views.

title: Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps
authors: Martin Tutek; Fateme Hashemi Chaleshtori; Ana Marasovic; Yonatan Belinkov; Christos Christodoulopoulos; Tanmoy Chakraborty; Carolyn Rose; Violet Peng
task_description: Erase information corresponding to reasoning steps from model parameters and measure the resulting change in predictions as a parametric faithfulness test.
inputs: Generated CoT steps; model parameters; MCQA instances
outputs_or_labels: Prediction change after step unlearning; faithfulness judgments
artifact_access_status: paper_and_PDF_accessible; artifact not confirmed in inspected evidence
evidence_basis: ACL abstract reports four LMs, five MCQA datasets, and unlearning key steps to test whether CoT is reflected in parametric beliefs.
limitations: Expensive and invasive for production pipelines; tests parametric storage, not whether a context engine preserved explicit provenance.
why_relevant: Useful as a high-cost external validity check: selected/compressed reasoning should not be the only evidence of dependence.

title: FACT-E: Causality-Inspired Evaluation for Trustworthy Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
authors: Yuxi Sun; Aoqi Zuo; Haotian Xie; Wei Gao; Mingming Gong; Jing Ma; Maria Liakata; Viviane P. Moreira; Jiajun Zhang; David Jurgens
task_description: Use controlled perturbations as an instrumental signal for intra-chain step dependence, jointly with CoT-to-answer consistency.
inputs: Reasoning trajectories; controlled perturbations; GSM8K, MATH, CommonsenseQA
outputs_or_labels: Intra-chain faithfulness; answer consistency; trajectory selection quality
artifact_access_status: paper_and_PDF_accessible; artifact not confirmed in inspected evidence
evidence_basis: ACL abstract says controlled perturbations separate genuine step dependence from bias artifacts and detects flawed reasoning under noise.
limitations: Requires careful perturbation operators and may be domain-specific; no natural-language scholarly provenance layer.
why_relevant: Strong model for edge-level deletion/substitution tests on proof or dialectical skeletons, not just final-answer accuracy.

title: Interventional Grounding Audits: Black-Box Premise-Dependency Tests for LLM Chain-of-Thought via Predicate Substitution
task_description: Substitute one premise predicate with a fresh symbol, rerun the model, and compare normalized conclusions against gold proof-tree dependencies.
inputs: ProntoQA problems; gold proof trees; generated reasoning steps; single-premise interventions
outputs_or_labels: Dependency detection F1/recall; audit certificates; right-answer-wrong-reasoning rate
pipeline_gap_filled: black-box dependency removal/substitution with executable gold structure
artifact_access_status: paper_and_public_repository_claimed; exact repository URL not verified
evidence_basis: arXiv abstract reports predicate substitution, proof-tree dependency detection, and public audit artifacts.
limitations: Formal parsability and synthetic entities limit transfer to implicit warrants and historical arguments; source URL needs pinning.
why_relevant: Most direct recipe for testing whether a generated step actually depends on the retained premise/span it cites.

title: Exploring the Limits of Fine-grained LLM-based Physics Inference via Premise Removal Interventions
authors: Jordan Meadows; Tamsin James; André Freitas
task_description: Evaluate step-wise physics derivation generation while progressively omitting supporting premises and manually judge mathematical coherence.
inputs: 1,200 derivation steps over 218 graduate-level physics derivations; premise/goal prompts
outputs_or_labels: ROUGE/BLEU/GLEU; accuracy versus S=0/1/2 removals; manual coherence
pipeline_gap_filled: graded dependency-removal curves and non-linear failure localization
evidence_basis: ACL paper reports curated derivations, controllable premise-removal intervention, non-linear degradation, and manual evaluation of 300 derivations.
limitations: Physics equations are more explicit than scholarly warrants; automatic overlap scores can miss valid alternate derivations.
why_relevant: Provides a concrete removal-strength ladder and manual fallback for cases where alternate valid reasoning paths exist.

title: MoPS: Modular Story Premise Synthesis for Open-Ended Automatic Story Generation
authors: Yan Ma; Yu Qiao; Pengfei Liu
task_description: Construct outputs from ordered modules with explicit dependencies, then ablate module dependencies to test whether sequential structure is necessary for coherent generated premises.
inputs: Nested module dictionary; selected key paths; generated premises/stories
outputs_or_labels: Completeness, coherence, diversity, originality; ablation degradation
pipeline_gap_filled: composition-level module dependency and order ablation
evidence_basis: ACL paper states modules such as persona depend on background/theme and that sequential dependencies are tested in ablation; code and generated data are supplied in supplement.
limitations: Story quality is not inferential validity; module dependency graph is authored rather than recovered from source evidence.
why_relevant: Useful protocol for isolating extraction→selection→rendering composition and testing order/dependency loss at intermediate stages.

title: What Makes Chain-of-Thought Prompting Effective? A Counterfactual Study
authors: Aman Madaan; Katherine Hermann; Amir Yazdanbakhsh; Houda Bouamor; Juan Pino; Kalika Bali
task_description: Systematically manipulate symbols, patterns, correctness, and intermediate steps in few-shot exemplars, then measure downstream behavior.
inputs: Few-shot prompt examples; counterfactual edits; multiple LLMs
outputs_or_labels: Accuracy deltas by manipulated component; mechanism findings
artifact_access_status: paper_and_PDF_accessible; artifact not confirmed in inspected evidence
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states systematic manipulation of prompt elements and tests consequences across three LLMs.
limitations: Prompt-example effects differ from deployed pipeline component removal; no provenance graph or scholarly corpus.
why_relevant: Template for paired intervention cells that separate semantic content, structural pattern, and surface realization effects.

title: LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
task_description: Retrieve premises from a formal library for proof states and test proof completion with executable checking, exposing which premises are available and used.
inputs: Lean proof states; Mathlib premises; theorem/proof trajectories
outputs_or_labels: Premise retrieval recall; proof completion; executable proof validity
pipeline_gap_filled: dependency-preserving selection and removal with formal oracle
license_status: Repository reports MIT; dataset terms require pinning
evidence_basis: Primary paper/repository identify premise selection, retrieval, and executable Lean checking.
limitations: Formal language lacks implicit warrants, rhetorical support/attack, and source provenance.
why_relevant: Best hard-control layer for whether selected context is sufficient, with exact proof failure rather than judge-only scores.

title: ProofWriter: Generating Implications, Proofs, and Abductive Statements over Natural Language
authors: Bryan Tafjord; Bhavana Dalvi Mishra; Peter Clark
task_description: Generate controlled rule theories with explicit proof chains, vary proof depth and open/closed-world assumptions, and evaluate entailment, contradiction, unknown, and abduction.
inputs: Rule theories; natural-language facts/rules; proof-depth variants
outputs_or_labels: Truth labels; proof chains; depth; abductive statements
evidence_basis: Primary paper and local corpus identify enumerated proofs, implication reasoning, abduction, and depth controls.
limitations: Synthetic rules underrepresent scholarly discourse and defeasible/support relations.
why_relevant: Provides a clean gold-dependency control and depth-stratified regression suite for the reasoning stage.

title: Distance between Relevant Information Pieces Causes Bias in Long-Context Language Models
task_description: Vary distance and positional arrangement among multiple relevant information pieces whose joint presence is needed for an answer.
inputs: Long contexts with distributed relevant pieces; position/distance conditions
outputs_or_labels: Accuracy/bias curves by distance and arrangement
artifact_access_status: official ACL/repository and local artifact verified
evidence_basis: Local dependency-compression record and official ACL/repository identify distributed relevant-piece interventions.
limitations: Does not label premise/conclusion edges; positional failure can be independent of semantic deletion.
why_relevant: Necessary control to distinguish true dependency loss from context-placement and attention failures after compression.

title: Goodhart’s Law Applies to NLP’s Explanation Benchmarks
authors: Jennifer Hsia; Danish Pruthi; Aarti Singh; Zachary C. Lipton
task_description: Construct adversarial explanation/inputs that inflate sufficiency and comprehensiveness without changing predictions or explanations, testing metric robustness.
inputs: ERASER/EVAL-X metrics; in-distribution inputs; adversarial explanation constructions
pipeline_gap_filled: adversarial validation of removal-based dependency metrics
artifact_access_status: paper_and_PDF_accessible; artifact not confirmed in inspected evidence
evidence_basis: ACL abstract reports dramatic inflation of ERASER metrics through out-of-support complements and label-encoding attacks on EVAL-X.
limitations: Targets explanation metrics rather than a full extraction/compression pipeline; exact attack implementation needs reproduction.
why_relevant: Mandatory hostile control: pair dependency-removal scores with distribution-preserving and adversarial checks before interpreting them as causality.

title: GRACE: Step-Level Benchmark for Faithful Reasoning over Context
task_description: Annotate and evaluate each reasoning step for source grounding and deductive/inferential faithfulness, with error categories and explanations across multiple datasets and model traces.
inputs: Human-annotated CoT traces from 10 models and 4 source datasets; source contexts
outputs_or_labels: Step-level faithfulness labels; error categories; explanations; inference and grounding tracks
pipeline_gap_filled: step-level dependency/grounding audit after selection or compression
evidence_basis: Primary arXiv record and official repository; retained local dependency-compression evidence
limitations: Does not itself intervene on a compressor or expose an explicit premise graph; source alignment is stronger than dependency reconstruction.
why_relevant: Provides a human-annotated step-level evaluator to localize whether compression-induced failures are grounding, inference, or unsupported-bridge errors.
